description: Plan 9.4 acceptance (X2.3). The plant is a pure bond graph (D28): IMs and IMu are the two I stores on the 1-junctions SJ and UJ, the suspension is the two-port SpringDamper Susp (20 kN/m, 1500 N*s/m) between UJ.a and SJ.b, the hard stop Stop (-/+0.08 m travel, 1 MN/m, 2000 N*s/m) sits on the same pair, and the tire is the project OneSidedSpring (copied from stdlib Spring; F = ifelse(x > 0, kt*x, 0), kt = 200 kN/m) between the road 1-junction RJ and UJ. The velocity source RoadV is driven by the stdlib TimeTable RoadProfile: a hold table with 13 samples at 0.1 s from t = 0.4 s, whose breakpoints 0.5/0.6/1.5/1.6 s give +0.5 m/s for 0.1 s at t = 0.5 s and -0.5 m/s for 0.1 s at t = 1.5 s, a 5 cm plateau bump. Gravity is the MSe preload (2943 N and 392.4 N) plus the static starts Susp/x = 0.14715 m and Tire/x = 0.016677 m, so t = 0 is the static equilibrium. design/design.py integrates the same equations independently (RK4, 1e-5 s) and prints every value below; the bond-graph run agrees to ~1e-6 m and ~1e-3 N. The plan's 5 cm bump peaks the suspension travel at 3.67 cm, so the hard stop never makes contact (Stop/a.e is exactly zero); the checks pin that bound and would fail if the stop were reached. The two mode frequencies are measured from the FFT of the free decay / ring-down (plan 9.4) and cross-checked by the zero crossings.

checks.note: static equilibrium: with the MSe preload and the static spring compressions the sprung mass does not move before the road input starts at 0.5 s
static equilibrium: the unsprung mass holds its ride height too
the suspension preload is ms*g = 300*9.81 = 2943 N: Susp/x starts at qs0 = ms*g/ks = 0.14715 m, and ks*qs0 is exactly the sprung weight
the tire carries (ms+mu)*g = 340*9.81 = 3335.4 N: Tire/x starts at qt0 = (ms+mu)*g/kt = 0.016677 m
the rising edge of the bump: +0.5 m/s from 0.5 s to 0.6 s
half of the 5 cm rise after 0.05 s at 0.5 m/s
the road reaches the 5 cm plateau at t = 0.6 s
the plateau holds 5 cm from 0.6 s to the falling edge at 1.5 s
the falling edge: -0.5 m/s from 1.5 s to 1.6 s
the road is flat again from t = 1.6 s
sprung-mass response 0.1 s into the 5 cm bump: the body has started to follow
the sprung mass reaches 7.465 cm at t = 0.893 s, i.e. 1.5 cm above the road plateau
just after the body peak
on the plateau just before the falling edge the body has come back to 4.75 cm
the body overshoots 1.8 cm below the flat road during the rebound
the wheel is on top of the plateau 0.05 s after the road stops rising
the unsprung mass peaks at 5.281 cm (t = 0.809 s), only 2.8 mm above the road: the tire follows the bump
the wheel is almost back on the flat road after the falling edge
the peak suspension travel from equilibrium is 3.67 cm at t = 1.615 s (rebound), less than half of the 8 cm free travel
the suspension travel never reaches the plan's +/-0.08 m hard stop (3.67 cm of the 8 cm limit)
-3.48 cm: the falling edge unloads the suspension
no hard-stop contact: the stop force is identically zero for this road input (the travel bound above is the guard)
the tire force peaks at 4.949 kN at t = 0.527 s, on the rising edge (the static load is 3.335 kN)
4.39 kN while the wheel climbs the bump
the measured minimum, on the falling edge: 1.673 kN, still 1.67 kN above lift-off
the tire force is never negative: TireNeg = min(Tire/F, 0) is identically zero, as the one-sided OneSidedSpring law requires
first upward zero crossing of the wheel velocity; with the next one this gives the wheel-hop period
second crossing 0.08437 s later -> 11.85 Hz, within 0.5 % of the plan's 11.8 Hz wheel hop
free decay of the body after the bump (the road is flat from 1.6 s): first upward zero crossing of the sprung displacement
second crossing 0.8256 s later -> 1.211 Hz damped body mode, within 2.3 % of the plan's 1.24 Hz
plan 9.4: the dominant body mode from an FFT of the free decay (the road is flat from 1.6 s) is 1.224 Hz, 1.3 % below the plan's 1.24 Hz, inside the +/-5 % band

plan 9.4: the wheel-hop mode from an FFT of the first ring-down after the rising edge (0.65-0.85 s) is 11.846 Hz, 0.4 % above the plan's 11.8 Hz, inside the +/-5 % band; the zero-crossing checks above pin the same period

no solver failure, no causal conflict, no derivative causality (every I and every two-port storage is integral), no algebraic loop, no Generic bond island (the island adopts Translation through SpringDamper/HardStop/OneSidedSpring/VelocitySource) and no event-limit stop: the TimeTable lands on its 13 sample instants (79 condition-only firings in total), far below the 10 000 limit, and the run reports no diagnostics at all
